samir: Heads-up — Product wants to ramp Nebula beta in 2 weeks (public signup). They estimate a big increase in token-generation per request. Need a quick impact projection so we can decide reserve vs burst and whether to push a soft rollout.

jess: How big is the model and expected per-request tokens? Any perf numbers from model team?

kai: Nebula is a 13B variant but heavily quantized for inference. Perf bench from research: ~7.2k tok/s on an A100-80 (fp16 + optimized kernels) for typical seq=64/ctx=2048 traffic profile. Current canonical model (Orchid-v1) is ~3k tok/s on same hw.

olivia: Baseline numbers for context: current peak aggregate across prod is ~120k tok/s (all models), with ~40 A100s active in us-west and eu-west combined during peak. Avg seq len ~56. Current buffer for sudden spikes is ~+20% (autoscale + queued capacity).

samir: If Nebula replaces some traffic and also drives more generation per request, what are the worst-case uplift numbers? Product is estimating 2.5x request volume for the first week and 1.7x sustained after.

kai: Quick calc: if Nebula is ~2.4x throughput-per-GPU vs Orchid (7.2k vs 3k), but product volume increases 2.5x, net aggregate token/sec = baseline * (2.5 * (Orchid->Nebula factor) where factor ~ (per-request tokens or generation?). Let's simplify with tokens/sec: baseline 120k tok/s from all models. If 60% of traffic migrates to Nebula in week1 and Nebula has the higher per-request generation, we can estimate +220k tok/s on top of baseline -> ~340k tok/s peak.

olivia: Translating tok/s to GPU count: use 7.2k tok/s per A100 for Nebula. 340k / 7.2k ≈ 47 A100s dedicated to Nebula at peak. We also need capacity for remaining models: say 120k remaining / 3k ≈ 40 A100s. Total ~= 87 A100s at peak. Current active is 40, so net delta ≈ +47 A100s.

jess: GPU-hours/day calc?

olivia: If peak lasts 6 hours/day and off-peak average is 50% of peak for 18 hours: approximate avg GPUs = (87*6 + 44*18)/24 = (522 + 792)/24 = 1314/24 ≈ 54.75 GPUs average. GPU-hours/day ≈ 54.75 * 24 = 1314 GPU-hours/day.

samir: Cost ballpark: what's our unit cost for A100? Assume $3.50/hr (reserved discount applied to some pools) and $6.40/hr for on-demand dedicated in some clouds.

olivia: If we assume blended $4.0/hr (mix of reserved and on-demand/spot), then daily spend ≈ 1314 * $4 = $5,256/day. Over the 14-day beta that's ~ $73k. If we need extra headroom (scale to 120 A100s peak) that pushes to ~1800 GPU-hrs/day -> $7.2k/day.

kai: Region constraints: eu-west pool only has 12 spare A100s on our Dedicated cluster. We can route extra traffic to us-west or use temporary cloud capacity but that requires network egress and compliance checks (some customers in EU require data residency).

jess: Options to reduce peak: 1) Enable stronger prefix/KV caching for common prompts; 2) Lower max generation default for Nebula in public beta; 3) Canary rollout to limit concurrent sessions; 4) Fallback to smaller quantized variant (Nebula-lite) during surge.

samir: Any quick wins for immediate capacity without signficant cost?

olivia: Quick wins: bump autoscale policy to allow +60 A100s from cloud burst (we have contracts with partner zones), enable aggressive KV caching, and throttle long-running streams after 90s. Also schedule a reserved purchase for 32 A100s for 3 months if metrics hold.

kai: Runbook snippets:

```
# temporary autoscale tweak
kf autoscale set --pool=prod-a100 --max-instances 200 --cooldown 120s
# routing: prefer us-west for public traffic
route set --name nebula-beta --policy prefer:us-west,fallback:eu-west
```

samir: Can infra-bot summarize exact GPU-hour and cost numbers and create a short Google sheet we can share with Product & Finance? Put the assumptions in the sheet.

infra-bot: Summary created: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1NebulaCapacityPlan (assumptions tab included). Key numbers: peak estimate 340k tok/s, avg GPUs ~55, delta +47 A100s, estimated cost $5.3k/day, 14-day projection $73k.

jess: Note: if Nebula's average seq length is higher than expected (e.g., users run longer by 2x), all numbers scale linearly — plan for a stress test tomorrow.

olivia: Action items: 1) Load test tomorrow 09:00 PT with 2.5x request pattern (assigned: kai) 2) Autoscale bump to allow cloud burst (assigned: samir) 3) Canaries enabled by product for 10% traffic (assigned: jess) 4) Finance heads-up on provisional $100k cap (assigned: olivia).

samir: Thanks — keep updates in this thread, paste load test logs here. :rocket:
